toegepas.na: wat diere agter hulle aan trek
toegepas.rede_vinder: The circumposition is 'agter ... aan' plus 'trek'; written together, 'aantrek' means to dress or to attract.
toegepas.fout: 'aantrek' written as one word reads as 'to dress' or 'to attract'; the circumposition 'agter ... aan' is written apart from the verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Plain spelling fix with no change in meaning; the extra word is earned by a real fault.

toegepas.voor: trek 'n vrag baie swaarder as die karretjie s'n
toegepas.na: trek 'n baie swaarder vrag as die karretjie s'n
toegepas.rede_vinder: The comparative goes before the noun in natural Afrikaans; same words, same meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'n vrag baie swaarder as' puts the comparative after the noun, which copies English 'a load much heavier than'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comparative before the noun is the natural Afrikaans order; same words, same meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Op een slag' is the idiomatic Afrikaans expression; same word count.
toegepas.fout: 'in een keer' is a loose borrowed form where Afrikaans has the fixed expression 'op een slag'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Same word count, same meaning, and the idiomatic Afrikaans expression.

toegepas.voor: Die voertuig was nuut en die dier
toegepas.na: Die voertuig was nuut, maar die dier
toegepas.rede_vinder: Two clauses each with their own subject and verb take a comma (AWS 2017), and 'maar' makes the intended contrast between new and unchanged explicit.
toegepas.fout: Two clauses with their own subject and verb lack the AWS comma, and 'en' blurs the contrast the paragraph is built on.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma is required and 'maar' only states the new-versus-unchanged contrast the heading already makes; no word added.

toegepas.voor: Die pedale draai die ketting en die ketting
toegepas.na: Die pedale draai die ketting, en die ketting
toegepas.rede_vinder: Both joined clauses have their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma before 'en'.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Die pedale draai' and 'die ketting draai' are two sentences, so the comma before 'en' is required.

toegepas.blok: Geen dier om te voer nie
toegepas.rede_vinder: Both joined clauses have their own subject and verb ('hy staan', 'niemand hoef'), so AWS 2017 requires a comma before 'en'.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Hy staan stil' and 'niemand hoef' are two sentences, so the comma before 'en' is required.

toegepas.voor: perde of muile trek, en waarin
toegepas.na: perde of muile trek en waarin
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'En waarin' joins two relative clauses within one sentence, not two sentences with their own subjects, so AWS 2017 takes no comma.
toegepas.fout: A comma before 'en' between two relative clauses inside one sentence, which AWS 2017 does not take.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A plain punctuation fix in the definition that changes no word and no meaning.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Saamgeneem' is the standard written form; 'saamgevat' is colloquial.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Saamvat' is ordinary, plain Afrikaans for a Grade 4 reader; the swap is lateral.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Vervoer' is the natural verb for a vehicle carrying passengers; 'mense gedra' sounds like carrying them in your arms.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Dra' for a vehicle carrying people is natural and is used consistently in this lesson and its definitions, and the next sentence's 'ook die pos gedra' leans on it.

laat_vaar.blok: Vroeë fietse en fietse van vandag
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Reguit' means straight (in direction); 'direk' says the pedals were fixed straight onto the wheel, which is the meaning here.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Reguit daaraan' already means attached directly to the wheel and is the plainer word for a Grade 4 reader; the swap is lateral.

na_skrywer.voor: wat perde of muile getrek het
na_skrywer.na: wat deur perde of muile getrek is
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: As written, 'wat' can be read as the subject, so the coach pulls the horses; the passive removes the ambiguity for one extra word.
na_skrywer.fout: 'wat perde of muile getrek het' can be read with the vehicle (or its wheels) as the one doing the pulling.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The ambiguity is real, but the same active pattern sits in the shared definitions of koets, wa and karretjie, so fixing only this sentence makes the lesson text and its definitions differ; the writer should settle it for the text and the definitions together.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: 'n Klein voertuig met twee wiele wat diere trek ... / 'n Groot voertuig met vier wiele wat diere trek ... / 'n Voertuig met twee wiele wat die ryer met pedale aandryf.
vlae.rede: In each definition 'wat' can be read as the subject and attaches next to 'wiele', so a literal reading says the wheels pull the animals or drive the rider. A passive form ('wat deur diere getrek word', 'wat die ryer met pedale aandryf' recast) would fix it but adds words near the ceiling and touches definitions that may be shared, so this is left for the reviewer or writer to decide.
